Maya: Ran a focused INT8 weight-only bakeoff comparing bitsandbytes (bnb) and llm.int8 on Aurora-13B. Quick summary: llm.int8 edges bnb on QA F1 (+0.8), but bnb gives ~12-18% lower p50 latency. Posting raw numbers + ops notes so we can decide rollout profile.
Li: Nice — can you paste the exact configs and numbers?
Maya: Yep. Setup: 1k-prod-like QA slice, single-node Aurora-13B (A100-ish), warm cache for steady-state. bitsandbytes v0.40 weight-only int8 with group_size=128; llm.int8 using our local transformer patch (recipe v2). Baseline fp32 for reference. Results below.
```
Model      | p50_latency(ms/gen) | tokens/s | QA F1
fp32       | 420                 | 75       | 83.2
bnb INT8   | 230                 | 137      | 82.1
llm.int8   | 260                 | 121      | 83.0
```
Ash: So perf vs quality tradeoff is small-ish on F1 but noticeable on latency. Any qualitative regressions/hallucinations?
Maya: We saw a small uptick in hallucination cases for bnb on long answers (~+0.4% on our metric). Also one tokenizer edge-case where bnb produced a trailing control char sequence in ~3 examples. Reproducer snippet:
```
python run_eval.py --model aurora-13b --quant bnb --group-size 128 --batch 4 --prompt-file qa_slice_1k.jsonl
```
Owen: @Maya can you propose a canary/rollout plan? Ops can add auto-fallback to fp32 if quality drops beyond threshold.
Maya: Proposed rollout: 5% canary for bnb in low-latency regions, monitor QA F1 + hallucination rate. If F1 drop > 1.0 or hallucination delta > 0.7% vs fp32, route to llm.int8; if llm.int8 fails, fallback to fp32. Will add eval-bot gates.
eval-bot: Automated eval scheduled: job eval-3921 queued (will run full diffs and confidence intervals).
Sara: Add commit hashes + seeds to the PR. bnb used commit a1b2c3 and flags: --bnb-quantizer=qint8 --group-size=128. llm.int8 used patch r42 on transformers-4.x.
Maya: I'll open the PR with configs, CSVs, and perf traces. Also adding a small canary runbook: 
```
route policy: {
  canary: 5%,
  monitor: [QA_F1, hallucination_rate, p95_latency],
  failover: [llm.int8, fp32]
}
```
Owen: Sounds good. Tag me when PR is up and I can schedule the capacity bump for the canary. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary started for model aurora-13b-bnb-int8 at 2498770000 — monitoring enabled.
Maya: Thanks all — will follow up with full eval diffs when eval-3921 completes. If anyone wants raw logs before PR, ping me. :party:
